text: In Malawi, 10 (23%) hospitals in 2001 and 14 (32%) in 2002 kept separate cross-border TB registers; their patients went unreported to the Malawi National TB Programme, neighbouring NTPs, and WHO, becoming missing cases. Cross-border new smear-positive PTB numbered 77 (2001) and 91 (2002) — about 3% of missing smear-positive cases in those hospitals, ~1% nationally. Quantitative time-lapse microscopy of Mycobacterium tuberculosis ribosomal RNA reporters revealed single-cell heterogeneity under standard growth, amplified by nutrient limitation, stationary phase, intracellular replication, and mouse lungs. Chronically infected mouse lungs harboured nongrowing but metabolically active bacteria, absent in interferon-γ-deficient mice and prominent under isoniazid, implicating them in latency and post-chemotherapy relapse. In 326 Korean cancer survivors (>1 year post-treatment) from 6 oncology clinics, knowledge, attitudes, perceived risk, and second primary cancer screening practices were assessed by multivariate logistic regression.
